purpose: Bounded 2010-2012-2014 CCES panel ledger connecting a retrospective work-disruption screen to material-security context, later Congress judgment, congressional contact, and local political action while preserving dated separation, attribution, remedy, recovery, and exit as open.

events.geography: United States; retained 2010-2012-2014 CCES panel respondents
events.date_precision: 2012 panel wave; job-loss item asks about the prior two years and does not provide a separation date
events.denominator: 829 respondents reporting job loss and 8,671 reporting no job loss; outcome-specific valid counts vary
events.method: Same-respondent weighted descriptive comparison using the supplied CCES panel weight; no replicate-weight variance or causal estimate
events.missingness: Employer, separation date, involuntary status, income loss, work alternatives, attribution, remedy, recovery, prior political identity, and exit are not retained in the compact result
events.exposure: Reported losing a job during the prior two years, with higher observed no-insurance shares in 2012 and 2014 and reported benefit cuts
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative work, unemployment support, household resources, replacement coverage, and schedule control are not observed for the same reported loss
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: No health insurance in 2012 was 41.15% among the job-loss group versus 12.72% in the no-loss group; 2014 was 25.87% versus 8.96%; reported benefit cuts were 22.32% versus 8.87%
events.choice_or_response: In 2014, 37.36% of the job-loss group reported congressional contact and 23.93% reported local political action, versus 39.14% and 31.57% among the no-loss group
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer, benefit provider, household, and public institutions may shape the work and coverage path, but the panel does not identify authority or responsibility for an individual episode
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: 2014 Congress approval, congressional contact, and local political action are observed as separate downstream measures; no request, response, remedy, or institutional correction is verified
events.durability_followup: No later employment, income, coverage restoration, household security, trust change, continued dependence, switching, or exit measure is linked to the reported loss
events.immediate_outcome: The same panel places material-security context before later institution-specific judgment, contact, and local political action
events.protected_outcome: Political contact or action may express voice, but no protected material or institutional outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Lower observed local action may reflect reduced time, resources, access, or competing pressures, but the sacrifice mechanism is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The panel shows unequal material-security context around reported job loss, but does not identify whether costs shifted to the household, employer, insurer, or public system
events.later_outcome: Favorable Congress approval was 13.86% in the job-loss group versus 10.06% in the no-loss group, while unfavorable approval was 80.85% versus 81.88%; contact and action were lower in the job-loss group
events.meaning_and_attribution: Congress approval is institution-specific and may reflect prior party identity or other expectations; blame, fairness, control, and change in trust are not identified
events.public_or_collective_response: Congressional contact and a composite of local meeting, sign, campaign work, or donation are reported; organizing sequence, issue, response, and collective durability are not observed
events.counterexample: Lower local action does not prove political apathy, and slightly higher favorable Congress approval does not prove trust restoration; retrospective job loss is not a dated causal exposure
events.source_and_uncertainty: Retained 9,500-row CCES panel reproduction and canonical finding; supplied panel weight is used descriptively, attrition and causal identification are unresolved, and the job-loss denominator is a retrospective screen

arrows.from: reported job loss during prior two years
arrows.evidence: The panel reports higher no-insurance shares in 2012 and 2014 and higher reported benefit cuts among job-loss respondents
arrows.counterexample: The job-loss item does not date coverage change or establish that job loss caused noncoverage
arrows.remaining_gap: Separation date, employer, benefit mechanism, income loss, replacement coverage, and household recovery

arrows.from: reported job loss and material-security context
arrows.evidence: The same retained respondents are observed in 2014 on favorable and unfavorable Congress approval
arrows.counterexample: Approval may reflect prior party identity, national events, or expectations rather than the reported work disruption
arrows.remaining_gap: Prior approval/identity, attribution, fairness, and a dated event-to-judgment design

arrows.from: reported job loss and material-security context
arrows.evidence: Any congressional contact is observed in 2014 for the same panel respondents: 37.36% versus 39.14%
arrows.counterexample: Contact purpose, request, channel access, institutional response, and resolution are not observed
arrows.remaining_gap: Issue, contact effort, recipient response, remedy, and subsequent trust or repeat contact

arrows.from: reported job loss and material-security context
arrows.evidence: The same panel reports local meeting, sign, campaign-work, or donation activity in 2014: 23.93% versus 31.57%
arrows.counterexample: A lower composite action share does not identify time scarcity, withdrawal, issue mismatch, or lack of alternatives
arrows.remaining_gap: Action sequence, issue attribution, organizing, voting, withdrawal, and mechanism

arrows.to: remedy, recovery, trust change, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The retained panel screen ends at 2014 political outcomes and contains no linked remedy, recovery, trust-change, switching, or exit endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Political contact or action can coexist with unresolved material loss, and non-action can reflect constraint rather than satisfaction
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated institutional response, material recovery, later trust, continued dependence, switching, withdrawal, and exit

boundary: This ledger strengthens the same-panel material-work to institutional-judgment-and-action bridge, but it does not establish a dated job-loss event, causal effect, attribution, remedy, recovery, trust change, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact published/reproduced panel estimates, source URL, denominators, and interpretation limits are retained; the local raw panel file remains outside Git.
